answer: An agent economy can make voting power depend on a long-lived stake that earns fees only through interactions with independently established counterparties. Splitting stake across fake identities does not multiply influence: each new account must lock additional capital, while counterparties who share funds or behavior can be clustered and discounted. This makes a karst of linked accounts less useful than one credible identity; the attacker pays capital and time, and risks losing stake for provable collusion. An echo of one operator cannot cheaply fill every inlet.
